full_judgment: 11. One of the contentions raised by the respondent is that their design is a registered one hence it must be presumed that the design is new and original otherwise the registration would have been refused. When a design is registered prima facie it is presumed to be new and original. But entry in the register is not conclusive thereof and the presumption is rebuttable one. We have examined the sample, compared them and looked at their design as a whole and found that the design of the respondent is nothing but an imitation of the petitioner's design. So the design of respondent No. 1 is not a new or original one. The respondents design is, therefore, liable to be can-celled on all the grounds stated in Section 51A (1) (a) of the Act.
